title: Top 5 BEST Civs for Beginners in AoE4

snippets.text: Age of Empires IV now has 23
civilizations and two more are coming
later this year, the Vikings and the
Scots. And picking your first civs in
AoE IV can therefore be quite
overwhelming, especially if you're a
beginner.
So, in this video, I will help you find
the best beginner civ for you.
The Abbasid Dynasty. Coming in at number
five is the Abbasid Dynasty. Abbasid
Dynasty is an economic civilization that
allows you to play two town center in
feudal, defend yourself, and then go
into castle age with a massive infantry,
typically ghulams, spears, crossbows,
and archers. They will be your go-tos.
But, the civilization also has a benefit
in its camel archer and camel rider
unit. The camel archers in the feudal
age will allow you to kill heavy tag
units like men-at-arms and knights when
you're fighting against either an age
two or even an age three opponent. The
camel riders in age four, when fully
buffed with all the bonuses from golden
age and the unique upgrades, prove to be
some of the very best and most
cost-efficient and high-quality units of
any late game army in both one-v-ones
and in team games.
The Abbasid game plan is simple. Get to
feudal with economic wing, build a
second town center on gold or deer, then
go to castle age if your opponent does
it, and make units. Sometimes, you want
to stay in feudal. If your opponent is
attacking you, your archer defense is
very strong.
They also benefit from composite bows
when aging up with military wing.
As long as you stay alive with the
civilization and you don't lose too many
economic units or army units, you will
usually always win in the end as your
second TC becomes a timer on your
opponent.
The Holy Roman Empire.
At number four, we have the Holy Roman
Empire, also better known as the HRE.
The HRE is a far more simple but
powerful economic civ that benefits from
a strong early economy through its
inspiration buffs and taking relics in
age three.
For a new player like yourself, this
might be the first time you come into
contact with relics. And when you play
HRE and grab these relics from the map,
you will really feel their bonuses shine
through them.
A tree gets stronger towers, keeps, and
wall fortifications from them by taking
a monk and placing the relic inside. You
get the gold, and throughout the game
that income will increase if you're
using the Rectness Cathedral landmark or
if you're getting the Tithe Barns H4
upgrade that allows you to get
additional resources from the relics.
It doesn't really matter where you put
the relics, whether it's in the towers,
in the keeps, or in the monasteries, it
will give you the same amount of income.
Besides its eco, its unit roster is
fairly simple but powerful. You have
access to the men-at-arms in the feudal
age, and with the Meinwerk landmark, you
can upgrade your spears and horsemen
with the special all pikes upgrades.
In castle age, you can have powerful
knights with Meinwerk, and in H4, you
can resort to spamming infantry or go
into black riders. You can get more
black riders by building additional
keeps. But most often, you'll see people
just spam infantry with a setup of like
15 to 20 barracks.
The civilization can best be summed up
as a civ with a powerful early economy
through the inspiration buffs from
prelates and the Aachen Chapel, and the
relic bonuses allow it to scale into the
late game, and therefore, it's a rather
simple but powerful civ.
Coming in at number three is the
Japanese. While technically being more
complicated than the HRE, the Japanese
main strategy is far more simple. You
will do what is called a fast castle.
Every game, you will play the same
strategy. Open on barracks, then you
will go feudal age with only one
villager building your landmark, and
while you build one or two towers on
gold, and then immediately castle age
with enough food and gold after
constructing your feudal age landmark,
then you'll be able to go castle and get
your bonuses. This is where you will get
your power spike through the Yabusame
and your unique units.
As Japan, you want to spam out a
samurai, a powerful and very upgradeable
knight through the Bannerman system and
the extra blacksmith upgrades. You place
a Yabusame from your H3 landmark inside
stable, get your TC upgraded to Daimyo
for the Bannerman buff, and then make
archers and knights and sometimes
spearmen until you win the game.
Japan can also be played as an infantry
civilization in the Feudal Age using its
free farms and berry buff to boost your
food income.

spear, and the archer Yumi Ashigaru.
Fully upgrade your units and roll over
your opponent.
Japan is a hard civ to counter for the
low and mid leagues as you need to have
very good attack timings against it.
Japan therefore thrives as a
civilization that wins on its build
order timings. So, if you practice your
build order timings in the skirmish and
you take them onto the ladder and you
have your timings right, then you will
be able to collect your due ELO points.
Speaking of collecting ELO points, it is
time to talk about the French that comes
in at number two.
The French, widely regarded as the most
hated civ in the low leagues because of
their knight spam in Feudal, are just
that strong as well. The French knight
is able to heal in Feudal Age. It has a
powerful damage boost after charging.
And if you keep enough of them alive and
never lose your knights, you can upgrade
them for very cheap.
The French are easy to play as their
main eco bonuses are passives. You have
faster producing bills. That's both
That's a bonus that will scale through
each age, become faster and faster.
And all your economy upgrades are
cheaper. That means you will have more
villagers and faster tech timings
compared to your opponents.
On top of that, your keeps will reduce
the cost of stable and archery range
units around them. And even better, you
have access to the Guild Hall H3
landmark that passively generates free
resources, allowing you to basically
just go H4 for free.
In H4, you have access to the most
powerful keep landmark in the game, the
Red Palace,
that replaces the main attack of your
town centers and your keeps with an
arbalest that absolutely murders anyone
who tries to raid you.
Pick French if you want to play a simple
and effective aggressive strategy in the
feudal age and skill check your
opponents. Be wary though, the civ
requires a bit of micro to execute, but
once you get a hang of knight archer
micro, you will have a lot of easy wins

The English coming in at number one is
no surprise to most people. It is a
close contender to the French as it is
one of the most hated civilization in
the game, especially at the lower
leagues. It is not as powerful at the
high levels, but as a new player, you
will find that this is perhaps one of
the most easy civilizations to play.
It's a classic in AoE 4 and is also the
most picked civ in low leagues. It has a
classic RTS identity of being a more
defensive economic civilization as your
town center fire more arrows and your
units attack speeds are buffed up when
enemies attack within TC or tower range
through the network buff. And your farms
are dirt cheap, making you able to play
the game without leaving the base since
those farms give you gold in the
Imperial Age as well.
Most players play two town centers into
fast castle with English. If you know
your build order well, you can have a
second town center down by around minute
4:50 and then go to castle age around
8:30, making you almost invulnerable
with good base building and placement of
buildings including your TC and your
White Tower H3 keep landmark.
Their unique units are the longbows, a
more powerful archers and their early
men-at-arms that come with additional
armor upgrades in the castle age. In
Imperial Age you can have wing guard
units with some pretty stats if you ask
me.
Or you can play the easy way and just
build the Berkshire and watch your enemy
panic as he gets shot from half across
the map.
Some more season players also like to
rush with English using either the
Council Hall to go for a longbow rush or
even attack in the Dark Age with
villagers and or men-at-arms. No matter
what, a well-timed early attack with
English can get you some really easy
elo.
